title: WooCommerce Review (2026)
intro: WooCommerce is evaluated here as an open-source commerce platform (plugin/core + extensions) — WooCommerce is an open-source ecommerce plugin for WordPress — free to install with costs coming from hosting, themes, extensions, and payment processing (WooPayments or gateways). Suited to merchants who want CMS + store control on their own infrastructure. No SaaS subscription for core plugin; extension bundles and Woo Express/hosted offerings are optional paid paths. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s Ecommerce methodology (ease of use, storefront/commerce fit, catalog & order depth, checkout conversion, integrations, omnichannel/POS, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose WooCommerce when WordPress ownership and extension flexibility matter more than an all-in SaaS admin.
verdict: Choose WooCommerce when WordPress ownership and extension flexibility matter more than an all-in SaaS admin. Consider Shopify or BigCommerce for hosted simplicity; Square Online for POS-led retail. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

faq.question: Is WooCommerce ecommerce software?
faq.answer: Yes. WooCommerce is evaluated as an open-source commerce platform (plugin/core + extensions).

faq.question: How is WooCommerce priced?
faq.answer: Free open-source core plugin. Budget for hosting, themes, extensions, and payment processing separately — no single all-in subscription like Shopify/BigCommerce.

faq.question: Does WooCommerce have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. No free trial is documented on the pricing page. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test WooCommerce?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
